messages.subject: Re: Controlling the number and values for labels using scale_area
parts:
I got this figured out. I ended up stepping back from qplot and
building up the plot in layers.


my original qplot: qplot(hwy, cty, data=honda, color=trans,
size=displ, geom=c("jitter")) + facet_grid( fl ~ year)

The ggplot components I built up:

honda_plot <- ggplot()
honda_point <- geom_point( data=honda, mapping = aes(x = cty, y = hwy,
geom="jitter", size=displ, color=trans), )
honda_facet <- facet_grid(fl ~ year)
honda_scale_size <- scale_size( to=c(3,4))


plot <- honda_plot + honda_point + honda_facet + honda_scale_size
print (plot)

Thanks to anyone who looked at this.

-- Adam

On Sat, Aug 27, 2011 at 1:24 PM, Adam Pridgen
<adam.p...@thecoverofnight.com> wrote:
> Hello,
>
> I am trying to use the scale_area function from ggplot2  in with
> qplot.  This is my third day of using R, so I am going to try and
> compose this question in a coherent.  If it does not make sense,
> please feel free in correcting me.
>
> I am trying to plot several distinct data points from the mpg dataset,
> and one of the data points is 'displ'.  My representation of 'displ'
> on this plot is the size of the plot.  Currently, my subset of data is
> mpg$manufacturer == 'honda' in honda (e.g. honda is a dataframe
> containing all the honda cars).
>
> When I try to plot the honda data set, the honda$displ size is very
> small, and I want to scale this size up with a constant, but I am not
> sure how to do this.  I attempted using "scale_area(to=c(3,8))"
> appended to my plot definition, but I ran into two problems.  First,
> the scaling does not correctly map to the honda$displ values, which
> are 1.6, 1.8, and 2.0.  The other problem I had comes from the legend
> having way to many values (e.g. 1.638, 1.690, ...).
>
> How do I control the scaling of continuous data points in a discrete
> fashion, and how do I control the number of legend entries in the
> graph?  Below I have included the code that I am using to form my data
> set, and then create and scale my plots.  I appreciate any help in
> advance.
>
> -- Adam
